subject: AstraMed marketplace invoice cutover & co-sell alignment
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@astramed.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: AstraMed marketplace invoice cutover & co-sell alignment

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the time today — great to learn more about AstraMed's rollout priorities. Per our call, your procurement team prefers to purchase via AWS Marketplace so invoices live on the cloud provider and match your internal chargeback flows. We can absolutely support that, and there are two practical paths:

- Cutover existing committed seats to an AWS Marketplace subscription (recommended for minimal service disruption).
- Keep the direct contract for now and add a Marketplace SOW for new spend (useful where commitments/discounts are involved).

To move forward I need two quick confirmations from your side:
1) Do you need exact price parity on the Marketplace SKU vs your current PO?
2) Who should we engage in procurement to accept the Marketplace terms (email for legal/procurement contact is fine).

I'll loop in our finance and marketplace ops to prepare an order form and the co-sell packet. If this looks good, can we target a November 1 cutover window?

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
D: +1 (415) 555-0198
[Attachment: AstraMed-MAP.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@astramed.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@astramed.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AstraMed marketplace invoice cutover & co-sell alignment

Hi Dylan,

Thanks — appreciate the options. A few clarifications from procurement:

- Price parity is required. We can't accept a higher list price in Marketplace vs our current contracted unit price; if there are marketplace-specific fees, procurement needs to understand net impact.
- Procurement would prefer the Marketplace invoice flow (chargebacks run via our cloud billing).
- Our legal prefers to sign a PO referencing the Marketplace subscription; they usually do not sign vendor EULAs directly.

Cc'ing procurement@astramed.com — Lydia Park from procurement will be the primary contact. Lydia, can you confirm any additional commercial/regulatory checks (e.g., SOC/SLA thresholds)?

Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, AstraMed
jordan.ellis@astramed.com
Phone: (202) 555-0134

- Marissa: start the co-sell packet and confirm if we need AWS ISV acceleration support for priority listing and co-sell enablement.

I'll ask Dylan (me) to send a draft SOW if needed, and I'll request DocuSign/PO flow details from AstraMed procurement.

Thanks — this is time-sensitive; Jordan is hoping for a Nov 1 cutover.

Dylan — all right, I put together the order form and pricing worksheet. Attaching the Marketplace OrderForm and a one-page conversion checklist. Key notes:

- We can mirror net unit pricing by applying the existing discount code on the Marketplace SKU (see line items).
- For Nov 1 cutover we'll need a signed order form or a marketplace subscription confirmation by Oct 25 to allow provisioning and billing sync.
- Co-sell: we should register AstraMed in the AWS ISV portal and request co-sell assistance; that usually takes 7–10 business days. Marissa, can you kick that off?

Dylan,

Thanks Ben — order form looks sensible. A couple of procurement items before we sign:

1) DocuSign vs PO: Our standard is to issue a PO referencing the Marketplace subscription. Can Redwood accept a PO that references the subscription SKU and lists Redwood as the provider?
2) SOC 2 / data handling: We need a pointer to your SOC 2 report and the support SLA. Can you send links?

Lydia (procurement) — we will accept a PO once we get the final order form and SOC evidence.

Jordan

Jordan / Lydia — great; next steps and timeline below: 

1) Order form & PO path: Ben attached the Marketplace OrderForm (AstraMed-Marketplace-OrderForm.xlsx). You can either:
   a) Sign via DocuSign (we will execute and then request AWS to enable the subscription), or
   b) Issue a PO referencing the subscription SKU and send to billing@redwoodinference.com. Both are fine; procurement preference is respected.

2) SOC 2 & SLA: link to our SOC 2 report: https://redwoodinference.com/security/soc2.pdf. Our standard support SLA is documented here: https://redwoodinference.com/support/sla. If you need a tailored SLA, we'll escalate to our security/compliance team.

3) Co-sell registration: Marissa will start the AWS ISV registration today. Expect a 7–10 business day window for co-sell clearance.

4) Cutover target: Nov 1. To meet that date, we need the signed order form or PO by Oct 25 and confirmation that AWS has accepted the subscription registration.

Action items:
- Jordan/Lydia: confirm PO vs DocuSign (reply by Oct 22).
- Marissa: share co-sell intake ticket ID when created.
- Ben: finalize invoice metadata mapping for the subscription.

I'll follow up with a DocuSign link if you prefer signature. Thanks everyone — aiming to make the transition seamless.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
